texts: mixed: the date, the joint 'together' reading, both groups and sundown all land, but 'the keepers of the East Row' falls into a hole in our instruction set -- a role noun with a live verb behind it can take either an of-phrase oblique or a possession link, and nothing selects between them -- and the kind atom saying the East Row is a row is missing beside its name, which is ours to fix rather than yours. Making the possessor a premodifier puts both phrases under a rule we do specify: 'On day 630 of Year 2, the East Row keepers together lit the East Row lanterns at sundown.' As in the other episodes, 'day 630' also sits outside the range our day term was written for -- again ours.
good. the burning comes out both as a group event and as a per-lantern rule that will fire on any lantern named later, with mire-essence consumed and linked to 'essence'.
good. 'together' correctly keeps this as one joint event with no per-lantern rule, and mist-light is linked to 'light'.
good. the showing gets the group event, the per-lantern rule and the night slot.

mixed: 'the mist-light' mints a brand-new thing instead of pointing back at the mist-light the lanterns produced two sentences earlier (there it was written as a bare kind word, here as a definite), so the chain from lanterns to moths is severed in the parse. Tie it to its source: 'The lanterns' mist-light attracted nightmoths.' -- or introduce it as 'a mist-light' in the producing sentence, after which a plain 'The mist-light' links back by itself.

mixed: 'a crowd of nightmoths' is indefinite, so it opens a fresh group with no link to the nightmoths the mist-light has just attracted, and the parse cannot tell they are the same moths. If they are, write: 'The nightmoths gathered in a crowd at the East Row.'
good. four sky-cats as a counted group, the descent as both a group event and a per-cat rule, and the cliff-spires as the source.

mixed: the group hunt, the crowd as its object and the crowd's location at the East Row all land, but the per-cat rule that a counted plural with a distributive verb owes is missing, so nothing follows about any single sky-cat. No rewrite is called for here -- your wording is exactly the case our instruction set already covers, so the omission is ours to fix.
good. the shrinking is predicated of the crowd as a unit -- the only sensible reading -- and it reuses the same crowd the sky-cats hunted.

mixed: 'some nightmoths' opens a new group with nothing tying it to the crowd, so the survivors float free of the set they came out of. Word it as a portion of that set: 'Some of the nightmoths in the crowd survived the hunt.'
good. 'the surviving nightmoths' reuses the survivors from the previous sentence, and the flight is carried as a group event plus a per-moth rule, with the Hollows as destination.
good. the same group reaches the Hollows, group event and per-moth rule alike.
good. the molting is tied inside the hunt by 'during' and distributed to each cat.

mixed: the threads, their silk property, the lanterns they were left on and the crowd as actor all land, but -- as with the hunt -- the per-moth rule owed by a plural subject with a distributive verb is missing. Again no rewrite is called for: the sentence is already the shape our instruction set covers, so the gap is ours.
